figure_inventory.description: Beige rounded box with a numbered list of 7 rows; each row = item name, dash, recorded weight, and an empty white square tick box at the right end (7 empty tick boxes, nothing ticked). Rows in order: 1. Iron Almirah - 40 g; 2. Bed - 60 kg; 3. Rice Bag - 5 kg; 4. Sofa - 30 g; 5. Bucket - 1 kg 800 g; 6. Water Bottle - 650 g; 7. Refrigerator - 50 g.

Coloured illustration of a pink-walled room, right of the list. Girl (Anu, pink dress, holding a notepad and pencil) stands in the middle. Objects drawn: dark two-door iron almirah (back wall left), blue armchair/sofa (left), purple bucket and a sack labelled 'BASMATI RICE' on the floor (left front), a bed with pillow and a small table with a purple water bottle and a glass (back right), a dark-blue refrigerator (right), a ceiling fan, a window with curtains, two framed pictures on the left wall, a tube light on the right wall. No weights or numbers are printed on any object.

Round analogue dial weighing scale (stopwatch-style brass-rimmed dial) standing on a tan base that carries a white answer box. A black arrow-shaped pointer starts at the centre pivot. Weighing starts at the red '0' at the top (12 o'clock); the pointer reads clockwise. Scale a: one full turn = 4 kg. Red '0' at the top with '4 kg' printed just below it; clockwise labels '1 kg' at 3 o'clock, '2 kg' at 6 o'clock, '3 kg' at 9 o'clock. Long ticks every 45 degrees (8 long ticks = every 500 g, the four labelled ones at 12/3/6/9 o'clock plus four in between); 4 short ticks between two long ticks, so the smallest division is 0.1 kg = 100 g (40 divisions around the dial; spacing measured about 9 degrees). Pointer points to the upper right, ending on the first short tick after the long tick at 45 degrees (the 0.5 kg mark), i.e. about 54 degrees clockwise from the top. Reading from the picture = 0.6 kg = 600 g.

Round analogue dial weighing scale (stopwatch-style brass-rimmed dial) standing on a tan base that carries a white answer box. A black arrow-shaped pointer starts at the centre pivot. Weighing starts at the red '0' at the top (12 o'clock); the pointer reads clockwise. Scale b: one full turn = 2 kg. Red '0' at the top with '2 kg' printed just below it; only one other label, '1 kg' at 6 o'clock (no labels at 3 and 9 o'clock). Long ticks at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock (every 0.5 kg); 4 short ticks between two long ticks, so the smallest division = 0.1 kg = 100 g (20 divisions, about 18 degrees apart). Pointer points to the upper left, onto the 2nd short tick counter-clockwise from the top (about 36 degrees left of vertical = 324 degrees clockwise). Reading from the picture = 1.8 kg = 1 kg 800 g.

Round analogue dial weighing scale (stopwatch-style brass-rimmed dial) standing on a tan base that carries a white answer box. A black arrow-shaped pointer starts at the centre pivot. Pointer points to the lower right, exactly on the long tick halfway between the '2 kg' and '3 kg' labels (about 150 degrees clockwise). Reading from the picture = 2.5 kg = 2 kg 500 g.

Round analogue dial weighing scale (stopwatch-style brass-rimmed dial) standing on a tan base that carries a white answer box. A black arrow-shaped pointer starts at the centre pivot. Round analogue dial weighing scale (stopwatch-style brass-rimmed dial) standing on a tan base that carries a white answer box. A black arrow-shaped pointer starts at the centre pivot.
